- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model may underreact; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to match sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overestimates; apply a 1–3% downward bias to align with true volatility.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% downward correction immediately after sentiment drop.
